- ai-legion: AI 后端调用：对已明确的单图 brief/参考图生成图片，或按明确任务调用外部 LLM 做文本分析、图片/视频理解。支持 Imagen、Codex GPT-Image 与 DeepSeek/Gemini；也接受上层 skill 的生成请求。不适用：整篇文章配图取舍（article-illustrator）、社媒系列图卡（xhs-cards）、需精确结构/文字的技术图（手写 SVG）、终端坐席治理；不凭「用 AI 生成」触发。
- bilibili: B站（bilibili）数据查询：搜索/读取视频详情、评论、弹幕、字幕、排行榜与 UP 主资料；对象为 BV号、b23.tv 链接或B站内容。读取数据，不负责创作/发布。

- web-fetch: 提取已知公开 URL 的正文；无专用适配器时统一选择轻量获取、Firecrawl、浏览器。专用平台/飞书资源先走专用 skill。不适用：未知 URL 搜索、多源调研（deepdive）、网页交互。
- wiki-compiler: LLM 专属知识库：原始素材编译成可检索的 wiki 文章；wiki 的事实账本把会议妙记与群聊抽成带时间和状态的决策 / 争议 / TODO / 时效事实，出每日增量日报和变更历史线；影响检查、回测、体检保证文章不过时。触发词：wiki、编译 wiki、ingest、加到 wiki、查 wiki、wiki status、compile、lint / verify wiki、事实账本、账本、fact-ledger、增量日报、导航日报、日报没发、决策记录、争议跟踪、TODO 跟踪、变更历史、回测、影响检查。边界：用户手写笔记归 knowledge-base；一次性群聊摘要归 chat-digest；调研本身归 deepdive；lark 系 skill 是底层 CLI。
- wx-cli: wx-cli — 从本地微信数据库查询聊天记录、联系人、会话、收藏等。用户提到微信聊天记录、联系人、消息历史、群成员、收藏内容时，使用此 skill 安装并调用 wx-cli。
- x-api: X (Twitter) 数据查询工具。通过抓包捕获的 GraphQL endpoints 直接调用 X 内部 API，无需官方 API key，支持用户资料、推文、时间线、书签、私信、通知、关注列表等。触发词：查 X 上的、Twitter 数据、推文详情、X 用户、书签、X 通知、X 私信、X 时间线、X 热门、X 关注、X 粉丝
- xianyu: 闲鱼 (goofish.com) 数据查询与操作。只读部分（搜索/详情/卖家在售/推荐）自包含；本机装了 xianyu-lib 后另有 IM 收发消息与 64 命令完整 CLI（发布/订单/物流/退款）。触发词：闲鱼、xianyu、goofish、二手、闲鱼搜索、闲鱼商品、闲鱼价格、闲鱼卖家、查闲鱼、闲鱼消息、闲鱼订单、闲鱼发货
- xianyu-listing-kit: 闲鱼快速发布素材生成 — 给一个商品 brief / 仿写一个 goofish URL / 或交互式问清需求后, 自动产出一组「图（PNG）+ 多版本文案 + 元数据」直接可上架。覆盖虚拟服务（Dify/智能体定制等 ¥100-¥1000 客单）和实物二手两类，内建副业雇主边界合规 lint（禁用词自动脱敏改写）。 触发：闲鱼发布 / 闲鱼挂单 / 闲鱼图文案 / 生成挂单素材 / 快速发布闲鱼 / xianyu listing / goofish listing / 帮我把这个商品挂闲鱼 / 仿写这个闲鱼 / 给我做套发闲鱼的图文案。
- xiaohongshu: 小红书（xhs）数据查询：搜索/读取笔记、Feed、评论与用户资料；对象为小红书链接或内容。读取数据，不负责创作/发布；文案交 writecraft，套图交 xhs-cards。
- youtube: YouTube 数据工具。支持视频搜索、视频详情、评论、字幕提取与分析、频道信息、播放列表。触发词：youtube、油管、YouTube视频、youtube搜索、youtube字幕、youtu.be、youtube评论、youtube频道
- zhihu: 知乎（zhihu.com）数据查询：搜索/读取热榜、问题、回答、用户、文章/专栏与话题精华；对象为知乎链接或内容。读取数据，不负责创作/发布；撰写或改写知乎回答交 writecraft，仅提平台名不触发。
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- workflow-authoring: Reference for writing a Workflow tool script (script API and gotchas, resume, quality patterns, worked examples). Load before authoring a script for a workflow the user already opted into; it does not itself authorize running one.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch
</system-reminder>

# Guabot — 常驻契约

一份文件三层：**默认**（§0）· **唯一常驻硬闸**（§1）· **场景规则**（§2，命中场景才生效，没命中当它不存在）。原 `global/rules/` 六份 2026-09-20 内化进 §2 后删除，逐字旧版 `git show dd9eb1d:global/rules/<name>.md`。Claude Code 不加载用户级 `~/.claude/AGENTS.md`（只认项目级，且 ≥v2.1.277），所以 `CLAUDE.md` 留一行 `@AGENTS.md` 垫片——正文只在这里改；Codex 经 `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` 软链读同一份。

## 0 · 每 session 生效

- **默认中文**：术语 / 代码 / 专名（git、worktree）保留英文，但不用英文写句子和标题。
- **报告多用视觉元素**：表格 / 列表 / 图优先；超 5 行纯文字先想能不能变表或列表。
- **开发规范**：Python 用 uv；JS/TS 用 bun；前端默认 React + Next.js + Tailwind。存量自带锁文件 / 流水线的不强迁。
- **优先派子 agent**：只要开子 agent 能提高效率——几件事互不依赖可并行、要扫很多文件 / 目录只需结论、长任务能放后台跑——就优先派 Agent（Explore / general-purpose / fork），主 session 只收结论不看过程；已知文件的单点查找、几分钟能完、需来回对齐的活自己做。

## 1 · 唯一常驻硬闸：以本人身份发飞书消息 / 邮件（send as user）

任何**以用户本人账号**把消息或邮件送进他人收件箱的操作前——`lark-cli im +messages-send/+messages-reply/+messages-forward/+messages-urgent-*`、`lark-cli mail +send/+reply/+reply-all/+forward`（未显式 `--as bot` 即按本人身份算，`defaultAs` 是 auto）、`feishu-cli mail send/reply/forward`（mail 域走 User Token）、lark-pb 的 `messages send / send / messages forward / gateway call`——必须先读 `skills/lark/references/write-gates.md`，按预览卡等用户字面确认；未读该文件禁止调用。**其他飞书写操作一律不需要确认，直接做**：`--as bot` 发送、`feishu-cli msg` Bot 消息、建 / 改云文档、wiki、drive、base、sheets、日历、拉群、reaction / pin。`hooks/lark-user-send-gate.sh` 只对上述本人身份发送弹 ask，其余静默；文字硬闸仍是第一道，禁止绕过。

## 2 · 场景规则

### 2.1 落盘产出物（文章 / 调研 / 对话捕获，skill 没定路径时）

根目录 `$NOTES_ROOT/10-Projects/`（`NOTES_ROOT` 读 `~/.agent-gateway.env`，未设回退 `~/SmokingMouse'Notes`）。AI 交互产出进 `ai-studio/` 按类型分目录、不在根目录平铺；学习 / 投资 / 量化等个人目录保持原位。代码 / 配置 / progress/ 等已有归属的不适用；新产出不知归哪 → 问用户。

| Skill | `ai-studio/` 下 |
|---|---|
| writecraft | `articles/{主题-slug}/`，**一题一文件夹**：落盘前先 glob 现有主题夹，命中就放进去、被取代的旧迭代移入该夹 `_archive/`，**不新建 v2 / jiedu 等并行文件**；细则 `articles/_README.md`。同级 `_drafts/`（在写 / 素材）`_archive/`（整篇废弃）`images/`（本地图源） |
| deepdive | `research/` 四区 by-wiki / industry / stocks / misc（分流见其 SKILL.md），`{slug}/raw/` 放原始数据 |
| research-report | 不新建目录：report.md + report.html 落被渲染档案同目录，旧版移 `_archive/` |
| stock-research | `research/stocks/{公司}-{YYYY-MM-DD}/` |
| wiki-compiler | `wikis/{domain-slug}/` |
| content-intel · content-ideation · storyboard | `intel/` · `articles/ideas/` · `articles/storyboards/` |
| xhs-cards | `xhs-cards/{YYYYMMDD-HHmm}-{slug}/` |
| book-distill | `books/{书名-slug}/`（distilled.md + raw/） |

**存储路由**（memos / Obsidian / story / Inbox 四方同一份；上行优先，命中即停）：

| 优先级 | 条件 | 落到哪 |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 用户**点名**存储（memos / Obsidian / daily note / Inbox / story） | 点名的那个 |
| 2 | 记的是**当前代码会话的上下文**（为什么这么写 / 决策 / 约束 / 交接） | `story` checkpoint（跟 git commit 绑定） |
| 3 | 用户说「**存一下**」这轮对话 / 这段回复 | `$NOTES_ROOT/00-Inbox/{主题slug}.md`，frontmatter `Tag: #Capture` / `Source: claude-conversation`（Codex 写 `codex-conversation`）/ `Date: {YYYY-MM-DD}` / `Topic: {主题}`，正文即回复 |
| 4 | 其余没点名目的地的裸速记（记一下 / 记个 todo / 备忘） | **反问**「记到 memos 还是 Obsidian」，不替用户猜 |

**格式**：给人读 / 分享 / 交互的产物（plan、审阅面板、报告 dashboard）可出自包含单文件 HTML，带闭环按钮（copy as prompt / JSON / diff）+ 内联 SVG（不走图床）；内部状态文件（progress/、wiki/）永远 markdown；不确定 → markdown。

### 2.2 进了有 `progress/` 的项目

起手读 `progress/README.md`（必要时 `git log`），告知进度 + 建议下一步。**只有 README 必读，其余一律 `rg`、不整读**；任何 progress 文件 >8 KB 禁止整读（`rg` 或按节 `sed -n`；Read / cat 整读会被 `hooks/progress-gate.py` 拒掉）。

| 文件 | 内容 | 怎么读 |
|---|---|---|
| `README.md` | Current Focus + Goals + 指针，<2 KB（hook 管） | 每 session 必读 |
| `sessions/<YYYY-MM-DD-HHmm>-<slug>.md` | 一 session 一文件，≤800 字符（hook 管） | 默认只读最近 1 个的 Next；用户问「之前怎么做的」才倒序翻 5 个 |
| `facts.md` | 已验证事实，每条带来源指针 | `rg` 关键词 |
| `failures.md` | 待查 ≤5 条 + 已结案（症状 / 可证伪假设 / 判定命令；出口 resolved · not-reproducible · expired，永不删） | 排查时 `rg` 症状 |
| `decisions/` | 重量 ADR | 开新方向前 `ls`，读命中的一篇 |
| `archive.md` · `decisions.md` | 已完成 Goal 一行一条 · 存量轻量决策，**不再新增**（闸拦写入） | 翻历史 · grep |

硬闸：
1. **Current Focus 一句话**：≤200 字符、无日期、无列表；活跃 Goals ≤3 条、每条 ≤160 字符。**Goals 由用户定义，不擅自增删。**
2. **一个 session 一个文件**：只追加本 session 自己这份，超 800 字符就把自己这份压回去；别的 session 的永不改。三段：`做了什么`（1-3 行；改了哪些文件看 commit 不写）/ `决定`（可空；每条前缀 `[decision]`，写清拒绝的备选）/ `Next`（1 行）。
3. **何时落**：session 收尾写一次、compact 之后补一次（§4）、用户说「记一下进度」——不预写、不中途反复改，**不是每次改完代码**；某 Goal 完成或变向时只改 README 那一行。
4. 通用坑写回 skill 的 Known Failure Modes（`skills/skill-creator/references/skill-management.md`），不进 failures.md；跨 session 的偏好 / 纠正走 auto-memory，不进 progress。存量 `sessions.md` 首次写新条目时 `git mv` 成 `sessions/0000-legacy.md`（直接写会被拦）。progress/ 只收上表的文件：除 facts / failures / archive / glossary、`decisions/`、`audits/` 外，写完 >8 KB 的文件会被拦——那是产出物，走 §2.1 或项目 docs/，progress/ 只留指针。并行 worktree 的可写集见 §2.4。

### 2.3 把一张图（截图 / 图表 / 生图）写进 markdown 或文档

任何 skill / 脚本产生的图片**默认上传本机 PicList 图床**（自定义域名 `img.smokingmouse.cc`，端口见 `global/workspace.md`），文档只引 `![alt](https://img.smokingmouse.cc/...)`，禁止 `./img/foo.png` 或绝对本地路径（跨机器失效，与图床 URL 混用 = 灾难）。
- 生成后**下一步**就调 `~/.claude/scripts/piclist-upload.py` 拿 URL 再写入，不先写本地路径占位后批量替换；所有 skill 共用这一个 CLI，不在 skill 内嵌 PicList API。
- 退出码 1（heartbeat 失败）= **终止操作**、提示用户启动 PicList 重试；**不允许**回退本地路径产半成品 markdown。
- 例外清单（写死，只能由用户扩）：① 临时测试图——不进任何最终产出物是唯一判据；② 用户说「先本地看 / 不发布」的预览图；③ 飞书画板缩略图（已云端）；④ 飞书导出素材（要在本地 md 引用时才传）；⑤ 私密 / 含未公开数据的图 → 留本地并标 `<!-- LOCAL_ONLY: 原因 -->`。

### 2.4 手开多个 session 在同一 repo 并行（worktree 工作台）

单 session 不需要。与 Agent / Workflow 的 `isolation:"worktree"` 是两回事——那是子 agent 的自动隔离（贵，仅并发写文件冲突才开），这里是操作者手摆多个交互 session。
- 统一落 `~/worktrees/<repo>/<slug>/`，目录名 = 分支名 = 任务 slug，主 repo 不受污染。建 `git worktree add ~/worktrees/<repo>/<slug> -b <slug>`；拆 `git worktree remove <path>` → `git worktree prune`。
- 任务完成回主 repo 本地 `git merge <slug>`（不走远端 PR），merge 前各 worktree 先把测试跑绿（证据附 file:line / 命令输出），再删 worktree。
- **铁律：并行期各 worktree 只写自己独占的文件**——`progress/blocks/<slug>.md`（该 session 的 Current Focus / 决策候选 / Next）和自己新建的 `progress/sessions/` 条目；共享单写文件（主干 `README.md` / `decisions.md` / `facts.md` / `failures.md` / `glossary.md`）**任何 session 都不碰**。merge 后**串行**收尾：Goal 状态进 README、方向性决策进 decisions、已验证事实进 facts，然后归档或删 block。
- worktree 只隔离目录不隔离逻辑：两边改同一批源码 merge 照样冲突，开之前先划清改动范围。

### 2.5 网页搜索 / 抓站 / 找相似内容，正在挑后端

| 需求 | 用哪个 |
|---|---|
| 语义 / 相似性（找相似文章、同类公司 / 项目、论文） | **exa**（neural 检索，独有） |
| 研究 fan-out 要直接可读的正文 | **tavily**（返回已提取正文） |
| 整站 crawl / map（站点粒度爬成语料） | **firecrawl** |
| 登录态 / 强反爬 / 本地 CDP | **`web-fetch` skill**，四家都替代不了 |
| 新闻时效 / 通用兜底 | 内置 **WebSearch** |
| ~~brave~~ | 未激活（要绑卡，且与 WebSearch 同质）；MCP 条目 2026-09-20 摘除（无 key 每局连接失败），激活步骤见 `global/workspace.md` 凭证表 |

**我要发……**：「写 / 制图 / 发布」是三件事，素材已生成 ≠ 已发布。博客 smokingmouse.cc → `blog-publish`（已核验：build + 上线验活）；飞书文档 → `lark-doc-polish` 排版 / `lark-doc` 落库，发消息另受 §1 约束；知乎 / 小红书 **暂无已核验发布入口**（`zhihu` `xiaohongshu` 只做查询，`xhs-cards` 只出图卡 + 文案素材）→ 成稿交还用户手动投递，**不要自称已发布**。

**配图 / 图表**：整篇文章要不要配、配在哪、配什么 → `article-illustrator`（编排层）；架构 / 流程 / 时序 / 分层图 → 手写 SVG / Mermaid，规范见 writecraft `pipeline/references/native-diagramming.md`；概念插画 / 封面 / 参考图生图 → `ai-legion`；评审时要可编辑 → `lark-whiteboard`；思维导图 → `mindai-chart-generation`；故事板 / 分镜 → `storyboard`。

原则：找不到对应薄编排就直接 `writecraft`，不为写一篇东西临时造 skill；文类知识住薄编排的 `references/` 或 writecraft 自己的 `domains/`；**改现有文档交付时必附 before→after diff**。

路径相对 `~/.claude/`；`global/` 不是封闭清单，按需 ls。

## 3 · Herdr 主控（herdr-leader）

`HERDR_ENV=1` 内遇到边界清晰、可独立外包、预计半小时以上且非交互的实现 / 调研任务，**主动提议**「要不要我以 leader 身份接管这个 workspace 来派」（`/herdr-leader`）；用户点头才进。交互性强、几分钟能完、需来回对齐的活不提议。

触发词：当 leader / 接管这个 workspace / 编队 / 让 codex review；旧称 焚决 / 派个坐席——**退役的只是称呼，运行时目录 `.fenjue/` 与 CLI `fj` 都还在用，别因「旧称」二字去改路径或命令**。

- Use multiSelect: true to allow multiple answers to be selected for a question

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

1 --- 2 title: Server and Client Components 3 description: Learn how you can use React Server and Client Components to render parts of your application on the server or the client. 4 related: 5 title: Next Steps 6 description: Learn more about the APIs mentioned in this page. 7 links: 8 - app/api-reference/directives/use-client 9 --- 10 11 By default, layouts and pages are [Server Components](https://react.dev/reference/rsc/server-components), which lets you fetch data and render parts of your UI on the server, optionally cache the result, and stream it to the client. When you need interactivity or browser APIs, you can use [Client Components](https://react.dev/reference/rsc/use-client) to layer in functionality. 12 13 This page explains how Server and Client Components work in Next.js and when to use them, with examples of how to compose them together in your application. 14 15 ## When to use Server and Client Components? 16 17 The client and server environments have different capabilities. Server and Client components allow you to run logic in each environment depending on your use case. 18 19 Use **Client Components** when you need: 20 21 - [State](https://react.dev/learn/managing-state) and [event handlers](https://react.dev/learn/responding-to-events). E.g. `onClick`, `onChange`. 22 - [Lifecycle logic](https://react.dev/learn/lifecycle-of-reactive-effects). E.g. `useEffect`. 23 - Browser-only APIs. E.g. `localStorage`, `window`, `Navigator.geolocation`, etc. 24 - [Custom hooks](https://react.dev/learn/reusing-logic-with-custom-hooks). 25 26 Use **Server Components** when you need: 27 28 - Fetch data from databases or APIs close to the source. 29 - Use API keys, tokens, and other secrets without exposing them to the client. 30 - Reduce the amount of JavaScript sent to the browser. 31 - Improve the [First Contentful Paint (FCP)](https://web.dev/fcp/), and stream content progressively to the client. 32 33 For example, the `` component is a Server Component that fetches data about a post, and passes it as props to the `` which handles client-side interactivity. 34 35 ```tsx filename="app/[id]/page.tsx" highlight={1,17} switcher 36 import LikeButton from '@/app/ui/like-button' 37 import { getPost } from '@/lib/data' 38 39 export default async function Page({ 40 params, 41 }: { 42 params: Promise<{ id: string }> 43 }) { 44 const { id } = await params 45 const post = await getPost(id) 46 47 return ( 48

The rendering work is split into chunks, by individual route segments ([layouts and pages](/docs/app/getting-started/layouts-and-pages)): 103 104 - **Server Components** are rendered into a special data format called the React Server Component Payload (RSC Payload). 105 - **Client Components** and the RSC Payload are used to [prerender](/docs/app/glossary#prerendering) HTML. 106 107 > **What is the React Server Component Payload (RSC)?** 108 > 109 > The RSC Payload is a compact binary representation of the rendered React Server Components tree. It's used by React on the client to update the browser's DOM. The RSC Payload contains: 110 > 111 > - The rendered result of Server Components 112 > - Placeholders for where Client Components should be rendered and references to their JavaScript files 113 > - Any props passed from a Server Component to a Client Component 114 115 ### On the client (first load) 116 117 Then, on the client: 118 119 1. **HTML** is used to immediately show a fast non-interactive preview of the route to the user. 120 2. **RSC Payload** is used to reconcile the Client and Server Component trees. 121 3. **JavaScript** is used to hydrate Client Components and make the application interactive. 122 123 > **What is hydration?** 124 > 125 > Hydration is React's process for attaching [event handlers](https://react.dev/learn/responding-to-events) to the DOM, to make the static HTML interactive. 126 127 ### Subsequent Navigations 128 129 On subsequent navigations: 130 131 - The **RSC Payload** is prefetched and cached for instant navigation. 132 - **Client Components** are rendered entirely on the client, without the server-rendered HTML. 133 134 ## Examples 135 136 ### Using Client Components 137 138 You can create a Client Component by adding the [`"use client"`](https://react.dev/reference/react/use-client) directive at the top of the file, above your imports. 139 140 ```tsx filename="app/ui/counter.tsx" highlight={1} switcher 141 'use client' 142 143 import { useState } from 'react' 144 145 export default function Counter() { 146 const [count, setCount] = useState(0) 147 148 return ( 149
150

{count} likes

151 152
153 ) 154 } 155 ``` 156 157 ```jsx filename="app/ui/counter.js" highlight={1} switcher 158 'use client' 159 160 import { useState } from 'react' 161 162 export default function Counter() { 163 const [count, setCount] = useState(0) 164 165 return ( 166
167

{count} likes

168 169
170 ) 171 } 172 ``` 173 174 `"use client"` is used to declare a **boundary** between the Server and Client module graphs (trees). 175 176 Once a file is marked with `"use client"`, **all its imports and child components are considered part of the client bundle**. This means you don't need to add the directive to every component that is intended for the client. 177 178 ### Reducing JS bundle size 179 180 To reduce the size of your client JavaScript bundles, add `'use client'` to specific interactive components instead of marking large parts of your UI as Client Components. 181 182 For example, the `` component contains mostly static elements like a logo and navigation links, but includes an interactive search bar. `` is interactive and needs to be a Client Component, however, the rest of the layout can remain a Server Component. 183 184 ```tsx filename="app/layout.tsx" highlight={12} switcher 185 // Client Component 186 import Search from './search' 187 // Server Component 188 import Logo from './logo' 189 190 // Layout is a Server Component by default 191 export default function Layout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) { 192 return ( 193 <> 194

See an [example](/docs/app/getting-started/fetching-data#streaming-data-with-the-use-api). 288 289 > **Good to know**: Props passed to Client Components need to be [serializable](https://react.dev/reference/react/use-server#serializable-parameters-and-return-values) by React. 290 291 ### Interleaving Server and Client Components 292 293 You can pass Server Components as a prop to a Client Component. This allows you to visually nest server-rendered UI within Client components. 294 295 A common pattern is to use `children` to create a _slot_ in a ``. For example, a `` component that fetches data on the server, inside a `` component that uses client state to toggle visibility. 296 297 ```tsx filename="app/ui/modal.tsx" switcher 298 'use client' 299 300 export default function Modal({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) { 301 return
{children}
302 } 303 ``` 304 305 ```jsx filename="app/ui/modal.js" switcher 306 'use client' 307 308 export default function Modal({ children }) { 309 return
{children}
310 } 311 ``` 312 313 Then, in a parent Server Component (e.g.``), you can pass a `` as the child of the ``: 314 315 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" highlight={7} switcher 316 import Modal from './ui/modal' 317 import Cart from './ui/cart' 318 319 export default function Page() { 320 return ( 321 322 323 324 ) 325 } 326 ``` 327 328 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" highlight={7} switcher 329 import Modal from './ui/modal' 330 import Cart from './ui/cart' 331 332 export default function Page() { 333 return ( 334 335 336 337 ) 338 } 339 ``` 340 341 In this pattern, all Server Components will be rendered on the server ahead of time, including those as props. The resulting RSC payload will contain references of where Client Components should be rendered within the component tree. 342 343 ### Context providers 344 345 [React context](https://react.dev/learn/passing-data-deeply-with-context) is commonly used to share global state like the current theme. However, React context is not supported in Server Components. 346 347 To use context, create a Client Component that accepts `children`: 348 349 ```tsx filename="app/theme-provider.tsx" switcher 350 'use client' 351 352 import { createContext } from 'react' 353 354 export const ThemeContext = createContext({}) 355 356 export default function ThemeProvider({ 357 children, 358 }: { 359 children: React.ReactNode 360 }) { 361 return {children} 362 } 363 ``` 364 365 ```jsx filename="app/theme-provider.js" switcher 366 'use client' 367 368 import { createContext } from 'react' 369 370 export const ThemeContext = createContext({}) 371 372 export default function ThemeProvider({ children }) { 373 return {children} 374 } 375 ``` 376 377 Then, import it into a Server Component (e.g. `layout`): 378 379 ```tsx filename="app/layout.tsx" switcher 380 import ThemeProvider from './theme-provider' 381 382 export default function RootLayout({ 383 children, 384 }: { 385 children: React.ReactNode 386 }) { 387 return ( 388 389 390 {children} 391 392 393 ) 394 } 395 ``` 396 397 ```jsx filename="app/layout.js" switcher 398 import ThemeProvider from './theme-provider' 399 400 export default function RootLayout({ children }) { 401 return ( 402 403 404 {children} 405 406 407 ) 408 } 409 ``` 410 411 Your Server Component will now be able to directly render your provider, and all other Client Components throughout your app will be able to consume this context. 412 413 > **Good to know**: You should render providers as deep as possible in the tree – notice how `ThemeProvider` only wraps `{children}` instead of the entire `` document. This makes it easier for Next.js to optimize the static parts of your Server Components. 414 415 ### Third-party components 416 417 When using a third-party component that relies on client-only features, you can wrap it in a Client Component to ensure it works as expected. 418 419 For example, the `` can be imported from the `acme-carousel` package. This component uses `useState`, but it doesn't yet have the `"use client"` directive. 420 421 If you use `` within a Client Component, it will work as expected: 422 423 ```tsx filename="app/gallery.tsx" switcher 424 'use client' 425 426 import { useState } from 'react' 427 import { Carousel } from 'acme-carousel' 428 429 export default function Gallery() { 430 const [isOpen, setIsOpen] = useState(false) 431 432 return ( 433

457 ) 458 } 459 ``` 460 461 However, if you try to use it directly within a Server Component, you'll see an error. This is because Next.js doesn't know `` is using client-only features. 462 463 To fix this, you can wrap third-party components that rely on client-only features in your own Client Components: 464 465 ```tsx filename="app/carousel.tsx" switcher 466 'use client' 467 468 import { Carousel } from 'acme-carousel' 469 470 export default Carousel 471 ``` 472 473 ```jsx filename="app/carousel.js" switcher 474 'use client' 475 476 import { Carousel } from 'acme-carousel' 477 478 export default Carousel 479 ``` 480 481 Now, you can use `` directly within a Server Component: 482 483 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 484 import Carousel from './carousel' 485 486 export default function Page() { 487 return ( 488

This lets your users import components into Server Components without needing to create wrappers. 514 > 515 > It's worth noting some bundlers might strip out `"use client"` directives. You can find an example of how to configure esbuild to include the `"use client"` directive in the [React Wrap Balancer](https://github.com/shuding/react-wrap-balancer/blob/main/tsup.config.ts#L10-L13) and [Vercel Analytics](https://github.com/vercel/analytics/blob/main/packages/web/tsup.config.js#L26-L30) repositories. 516 517 ### Preventing environment poisoning 518 519 JavaScript modules can be shared between both Server and Client Components modules. This means it's possible to accidentally import server-only code into the client. For example, consider the following function: 520 521 ```ts filename="lib/data.ts" switcher 522 export async function getData() { 523 const res = await fetch('https://external-service.com/data', { 524 headers: { 525 authorization: process.env.API_KEY, 526 }, 527 }) 528 529 return res.json() 530 } 531 ``` 532 533 ```js filename="lib/data.js" switcher 534 export async function getData() { 535 const res = await fetch('https://external-service.com/data', { 536 headers: { 537 authorization: process.env.API_KEY, 538 }, 539 }) 540 541 return res.json() 542 } 543 ``` 544 545 This function contains an `API_KEY` that should never be exposed to the client. 546 547 In Next.js, only environment variables prefixed with `NEXT_PUBLIC_` are included in the client bundle. However, if your linting rules flag extraneous dependencies, you may install them to avoid issues. 574 575 ```bash package="npm" 576 npm install server-only 577 ``` 578 579 ```bash package="yarn" 580 yarn add server-only 581 ``` 582 583 ```bash package="pnpm" 584 pnpm add server-only 585 ``` 586 587 ```bash package="bun" 588 bun add server-only 589 ``` 590 591 Next.js handles `server-only` and `client-only` imports internally to provide clearer error messages when a module is used in the wrong environment. The contents of these packages from NPM are not used by Next.js. 592 593 Next.js also provides its own type declarations for `server-only` and `client-only`, for TypeScript configurations where [`noUncheckedSideEffectImports`](https://www.typescriptlang.org/tsconfig/#noUncheckedSideEffectImports) is active. 594
